CA.name: Wild quinine
CA.citation: Wikipedia; NatureServe. Unrelated to true quinine (Cinchona spp.) despite the common name; distinguished from the invasive Parthenium hysterophorus (Santa Maria feverfew), which causes contact dermatitis

DE.name: Praerieampfer
DE.citation: Consistent name across independent German nurseries (Baumschule NewGarden, Stauden Stade, Floragard)

GB.name: Wild quinine
GB.citation: Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) plant record, listing common names "cutting almond, prairie dock, wild quinine"

US.name: Wild quinine
US.citation: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder; Lurie Garden. Used medicinally and as a poultice for burns by the Catawba people
